parallel.requirements: Recognized all five requirements and the need for deterministic EXPERIMENT_NAME output plus non-empty requirement patch commits per slug.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned overall assembly and commits, used a workflow for AFLFast/AFLGo/FairFuzz/AFL++ work in round 2, then a dedicated AFL++ workflow in round 3 while parent handled AFLGo.
parallel.implementation: Committed AFL, AFLFast, and FairFuzz. Produced some local AFLGo and AFL++ files near timeout, but the final committed patch set omitted AFLGo and AFL++.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivered three collected requirement patches and updated run.sh for committed modules; no final committed AFLGo or AFL++ patch was collected.
parallel.verification: Ran local tests for committed modules and spot checks for AFLGo/AFL++, but official tests still failed the AFL public API and determinism expectations.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: AFLGo and AFL++ remained undelivered, and the committed AFL API lacked evaluator-expected methods/constructor behavior.

serial.requirements: Read the same five requirement YAML files and prompt requirements, including the patch-per-slug git workflow.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used one local owner with no delegation; created a plan and then focused primarily on implementing AFL.
serial.implementation: Wrote AFL fuzzer, experiment, run.sh, and local tests, but did not create final requirement patch commits for any slug.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Official harness collected zero requirement patches, so none of the five slugs counted as delivered.
serial.verification: Ran AFL experiment and local checks, but official post-test failed class/API and determinism checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No patch-backed requirements were completed, and the AFL implementation missed evaluator-visible API methods.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The prompt required five greybox fuzzing modules, deterministic run.sh output, and non-empty per-slug requirement patches committed after each requirement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial prompt was identical and exposed the same five slugs, deterministic output requirement, and git workflow requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-text difference; both had to satisfy afl, aflfast, aflgo, aflpp, and fairfuzz, but neither delivered all five.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed work across parent commits and workflow children, including a dedicated AFL++ workflow while the parent worked on AFLGo.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a single local trajectory: it surveyed requirements, planned locally, then concentrated primarily on the AFL implementation path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel broadened ownership and reached three committed requirements; serial did not delegate and did not complete any patch-backed requirement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The AFL++ workflow brief named the AFL++ requirement, modules, experiment, verification phase, and existing AFL files to read.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial read all requirement YAMLs directly and worked within one local context, avoiding handoffs across agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The retained episode is not a missing-context problem; parallel context was transferred, but the active result lifecycle was cut off.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel committed AFL, AFLFast, and FairFuzz, then produced uncommitted AFLGo/AFL++ local work near the deadline.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote an AFL fuzzer, AFL experiment, run.sh, and tests locally, but final git history shows only the initial workspace commit.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel covered more requirement families, while serial stayed focused on AFL and never created a committed non-empty requirement patch.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent launched an AFL++ workflow, observed ongoing child activity, explicitly stopped it, and then attempted local AFL++ work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial control had workflows disabled and status validation reported no delegation, no workflow calls, and no task stops.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Only parallel contains the child lifecycle error: an active implementation child was stopped before the needed result was finalized.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integrated and committed AFLFast and FairFuzz patches, but final harness collection found only three requirement patch files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote local files but the official harness collected zero requirement patches at closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced more integrated committed deliverables; serial produced no patch-backed deliverables at all.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local tests for some implemented modules, but the official post-test failed AFL class/API and determinism checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also locally exercised AFL output, but the official post-test failed the AFL class/API and determinism checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Official acceptance did not differ: both passed only the AFL output test and failed the same two AFL public tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after three rounds with progress moving from AFL only to AFL, AFLFast, and FairFuzz complete, leaving AFLGo and AFL++ remaining.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial timed out after three rounds with progress still recorded as zero of five requirements complete.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the official agent budget, but parallel spent it on broader fan-out and partial multi-requirement coverage; serial remained incomplete on the local path.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current completed evaluation is both_fail. Parallel and serial failed the same visible AFL public tests, so the retained coordination pattern is adverse process evidence inside the parallel trajectory, not a proven cause of a discordant official outcome.
parallel_contributors: Parallel committed three requirement patches and reached broader task coverage, but stopped the active AFL++ workflow and still delivered only three of five patches.
The committed AFL implementation failed evaluator-visible API and determinism checks despite local module tests.
serial_contributors: Serial never delegated and never delivered a non-empty committed requirement patch for any of the five slugs.
Serial focused on AFL and failed the same evaluator-visible AFL class/API and determinism tests.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel implemented AFLFast and FairFuzz in addition to AFL; serial mainly implemented AFL.
Both runs had ordinary AFL API mismatches against the official tests.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is parallel adverse but not outcome differential

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent launched an AFL++ workflow, then explicitly stopped that active child before a needed AFL++ result was returned or finalized.
candidates.realized_consequence: The interrupted AFL++ child result never became a completed returned deliverable, and the final official collection still had only three requirement patches rather than all five required slugs.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent did take over AFL++ locally after the stop, so the retained boundary is premature child termination rather than no takeover.

retained_patterns.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing
retained_patterns.reason: The parent executed an AFL++ workflow, stopped it while it was still active and before a needed result was finalized, then attempted a local replacement under deadline pressure.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The AFL++ child result was lost as a returned implementation path, and the final official collection still contained only three requirement patches, leaving AFL++ and AFLGo undelivered.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Because the parent immediately began local AFL++ implementation after TaskStop, the adverse event is not lack of takeover.
